 (BY SHRI ASHISH KUMAR KURMI - ADVOCATE)
 AND  1. THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH P.S.
 BAHROL DISTT. SAGAR (MADHYA PRADESH)
 2. VICTIM A D/O NOT MENTION NOT MENTION  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 .
(BY SHRI MANOJ KUSHWAHA - PANEL LAWYER FOR THE
RESPONDENT
/STATE

This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.30/2022 dated 15.02.2022 registered at Police Station - Bahrol,
District- Sagar (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Section 363, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.

Applicant is in detention since 11.02.2023.
2.
As per the prosecution story, on 15.02.2022, 17 year old prosecutrix's uncle lodged an FIR about missing of his niece.
FIR was registered under Section 363 of IPC.
Almost after a period of one year of her missing, prosecutrix appeared before the police and that time she was pregnant.

After investigation, charge sheet was filed and prosecutrix evidence has been recorded before the trial Narendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61739916/
1 Court.
3.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
Prosecutrix is his wedded wife and the child delivered by the prosecutrix is his legitimate child.
At the time of commission of alleged offence prosecutrix was 18 years of age.
It is further submitted that prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
She has not supported the prosecution story.
As prosecutrix has already been examined, no question of influencing or tampering with the evidence arises.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail.
4 . O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant on the ground that at the time of commission of offence, prosecutrix was 17 years of age.
5. Before trial Court, prosecutrix has already been examined.
She has not supported the prosecution story and has stated that applicant is her husband.
There is no apprehension of tampering of prosecution evidence as prosexutrix has already been examined.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6 . It is directed that applicant - Narendra be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Jasleen Narendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023
